brief: Goldman Sachs FICC (Robert Quinn) on US diesel. Between September 1 and 8 prices underperformed because Russian and Middle East developments alleviated geopolitical risk premium: October ULSD slid 2.3%, term structure softened and crack spreads declined, with most crack losses following Russia's announcement that it would resume diesel exports conditional on a successful refill of domestic inventories. DOE distillate stocks surprisingly built and an Iran-Oman Hormuz passage deal moved closer. Managed Money was the largest seller, net selling $955mm, the most significant bearish flow since November 2025, of which long unwinds were 87%, with part of the bullish energy expression potentially rotating into RBOB gasoline or gasoil. Net diesel length still sat at an 83% two year notional rank. From September 8 to 11 the chase resumed as Middle East tempers flared: October diesel surged more than 8%, the front crack versus WTI reclaimed its high, and aggregate open interest added $1.9bn, signaling long reinstatement. Cited drivers are US destruction of Iranian tankers, attacks that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and Houthi advances threatening Bab el-Mandeb. Remaining supply-side focus: the Iran-GCC meeting, delayed US refinery maintenance, possible higher Chinese exports, and Russian runs below seasonal norms.
